title: DNS Concepts Practice
subject: DNS
description: Practice resolving common DNS problems using evidence-first triage, diagnosis, and fix decisions. Titles and summaries are symptom-based to keep the root cause discoverable during the workflow.
reportOverview: This report summarizes your ticket outcomes and change notes for DNS concepts practice. Use it to reflect on your decision path and evidence interpretation.
evidenceInstructions:
Instructions:
1) Read the observed symptom and scan the evidence.
2) Decide what you should verify first (Triage).
3) Choose the most likely cause based on the evidence (Diagnosis).
4) Select the best remediation action (Fix).
5) Write a short change note describing what changed and how you validated it.

tickets.title: New workstation cannot complete domain join
tickets.summary: A newly imaged workstation fails to join the domain. Internet access works, but the domain join wizard reports it cannot locate a domain controller.
validations: Confirm the client uses internal DNS (DC IPs).
Re-run SRV lookup for _ldap._tcp.dc._msdcs.<domain>.
Attempt domain join again after correction.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST on the affected workstation?
options: Which DNS servers the workstation is using (internal vs public)
Whether the workstation has the latest Windows updates
Whether the workstation time zone matches the domain controller
Whether the workstation has enough free disk space

diagnosis.q: Based on the evidence, what is the MOST likely reason the join fails?
options: The domain controller is offline
The workstation is using public DNS and cannot resolve domain SRV records
The DHCP scope is out of addresses
The workstation has a duplicate computer name in Active Directory

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Configure the client (or DHCP option 006) to use the domain controller(s) as DNS servers
Create a new reverse lookup zone immediately
Disable secure dynamic updates on the DNS zone
Reinstall the workstation network driver

tickets.title: Users cannot reach a file server by name
tickets.summary: Users can reach the file server by IP address, but attempts to reach it by hostname fail across multiple clients.
artifact: ping fileserver.contoso.com -> Ping request could not find host fileserver.contoso.com
*** dc01.contoso.com can't find fileserver.contoso.com: Non-existent domain
validations: Confirm the record exists in the correct forward lookup zone.
Validate resolution from multiple clients.
Confirm no conflicting records exist.

triage.q: What is the FIRST thing to check on the DNS server?
options: Whether an A record exists for fileserver.contoso.com in the correct zone
Whether the DNS server has forwarders configured
Whether a reverse lookup zone exists for 10.0.0.0/24
Whether DNS scavenging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause of the failure?
options: The server IP address changed and clients cached it
The hostname record is missing (deleted or never created)
A conditional forwarder is misconfigured
The DNS server recursion setting is disabled

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Create (or re-register) the host A record for fileserver.contoso.com
Add 8.8.8.8 to DNS forwarders
Disable aging and scavenging on the zone
Create a root zone named "."

tickets.title: A few users still see the old intranet after maintenance
tickets.summary: After an intranet cutover, most users reach the updated intranet, but a few users still reach the old site or old content.
artifact: IT confirms DNS zone now points intranet.contoso.com -> 10.0.20.25
validations: Verify nslookup returns the new IP on the client after remediation.
Confirm client cache no longer contains the old IP.
Validate intranet loads correctly.

triage.q: What is the FIRST troubleshooting step on the affected user PC?
options: Check the local DNS resolver cache for intranet.contoso.com
Restart the DNS Server service on the domain controller
Delete the intranet DNS record and recreate it
Disable the user’s firewall

diagnosis.q: Based on the evidence, what is the MOST likely cause?
options: The DNS server is using root hints instead of forwarders
The user’s machine has a stale cached DNS record
The intranet server is down
The reverse lookup zone is missing

fix.q: Which action is the best fix for the affected user?
options: Flush the DNS cache on the affected PC and retry
Authorize DHCP in Active Directory
Enable zone transfers to a secondary DNS server
Disable secure dynamic updates

tickets.title: Users cannot use the short intranet URL
tickets.summary: Users want to access the intranet using a short name (for example, http://portal) but it does not resolve internally.
artifact: *** dc01.contoso.com can't find portal: Non-existent domain
validations: Confirm the alias resolves to the correct target.
Confirm portal resolves from multiple clients.
Validate intranet loads using the short name.

triage.q: What is the FIRST check on the DNS side to support a short name like "portal"?
options: Check whether an alias record exists for portal
Check whether the DNS server has root hints configured
Check whether scavenging is enabled
Check whether the reverse lookup zone exists

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely reason the short name does not work?
options: No alias (CNAME) record exists for portal
The DHCP scope is exhausted
The DC’s time is out of sync
The DNS server is not authorized

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Create a CNAME record named portal pointing to webserver01.contoso.com
Create a reverse lookup zone for 10.0.0.0/24
Disable recursion on the DNS server
Remove the contoso.com forward lookup zone

tickets.title: Internal resources work but external websites do not resolve
tickets.summary: Users can access internal resources by name, but external names like google.com and outlook.com do not resolve across the organization.
validations: Confirm external nslookup succeeds from server and client.
Confirm internal name resolution still works.
Check DNS event logs for timeouts after fix.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST on the DNS server for external resolution issues?
options: Forwarders configuration (or upstream resolvers)
Presence of a reverse lookup zone
Whether the zone is AD-integrated
Whether clients are using DHCP reservations

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause given the evidence?
options: No upstream forwarders are configured, so external recursion is failing in this environment
The A record for google.com is missing from the contoso.com zone
Clients have stale DNS cache entries for external sites
The DHCP lease duration is too short

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Add valid forwarders (upstream DNS) on the DNS server and retest external lookups
Disable the DNS Server service and re-enable it
Delete the forward lookup zone for contoso.com
Disable secure dynamic updates

tickets.title: Security tool shows many devices as unknown by IP
tickets.summary: A monitoring/security tool lists devices only by IP and shows many as unknown, even though you expect hostnames to appear.
validations: Confirm reverse zone exists for the subnet(s).
Confirm PTR lookups return names.
Confirm tool can now display hostnames.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST to support reverse lookups?
options: That the correct reverse lookup zone exists for the subnet
That forwarders are configured
That DNS scavenging is disabled
That DHCP failover is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely reason nslookup by IP fails?
options: A reverse lookup zone (PTR) is missing for the subnet
The client DNS cache is stale
A CNAME record is missing
The DNS server is unauthorized

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Create the appropriate reverse lookup zone and allow PTR registration
Create a forwarder to 8.8.8.8
Disable the DNS Client service on all workstations
Delete all A records and force clients to re-register

tickets.title: External name resolution stopped suddenly after a change
tickets.summary: Internal name resolution still works, but external name resolution stopped immediately across the organization after a DNS-related change.
artifact: DNS Manager shows a new zone named "." (dot) under Forward Lookup Zones.
validations: Confirm external lookups succeed after removing the problematic configuration.
Verify internal zones continue to resolve.
Check DNS Server event log for recurrence.

triage.q: What is the FIRST thing to check in DNS Manager given the evidence?
options: Whether a root zone named "." exists on the DNS server
Whether DHCP option 006 is configured
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether the DNS cache is full

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely explanation for external resolution failing immediately?
options: A root zone was created, preventing normal recursion/forwarder usage
All external websites changed their IP addresses overnight
Clients have stale DNS cache entries for external names
The file server A record is missing

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Remove the "." zone and restart DNS service if needed, then retest external resolution
Create a CNAME record for "."
Disable secure dynamic updates in the contoso.com zone
Reduce DHCP lease duration

tickets.title: Secondary DNS server shows a zone error and no records
tickets.summary: A secondary DNS server was added for redundancy, but the zone does not populate and the console shows an error for the zone.
artifact: Forward Lookup Zones -> contoso.com shows: "Zone not loaded"
Zone Transfers tab: currently not allowing transfers
validations: Confirm the secondary zone loads and records appear.
Confirm secondary can resolve records from the zone.
Confirm zone transfer status remains healthy.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST on the primary DNS server for a secondary zone that won't load?
options: Whether zone transfers are allowed to the secondary server
Whether forwarders are configured
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether DNS scavenging is enabled

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely reason the secondary zone is empty/not loaded?
options: Zone transfers are blocked or not permitted to the secondary server
The A record for the DNS server is missing
The client DNS cache is stale
The DHCP scope is exhausted

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Enable zone transfers (to the secondary server) on the primary zone and retry
Delete the primary DNS zone and recreate it
Disable recursion on the primary DNS server
Change the DHCP subnet mask

tickets.title: DNS updates appear on one domain controller but not the other
tickets.summary: DNS records created/updated on one domain controller are not appearing on the other, even after an extended period.
artifact: - Record created on DC1 appears immediately on DC1
- Record does not appear on DC2 after 60+ minutes
DC2 Event Viewer shows Kerberos/Security related errors.
validations: Confirm time is synchronized across DCs.
Confirm AD replication is healthy.
Confirm DNS records replicate to the other DC.

triage.q: What should you verify FIRST when replication-related symptoms appear between DCs?
options: Time synchronization between domain controllers
Whether the reverse lookup zone exists
Whether forwarders are configured
Whether clients have stale DNS caches

diagnosis.q: What is the MOST likely cause based on the evidence?
options: Time drift is causing authentication/replication failures, delaying DNS replication
The CNAME record is missing for the domain
Zone transfers are disabled
DHCP is issuing duplicate addresses

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Correct time/NTP configuration and confirm replication resumes
Create a root zone named "."
Disable secure dynamic updates
Delete the contoso.com zone and recreate it

tickets.title: Cannot add DNS records from one server; option is unavailable
tickets.summary: An administrator cannot add new host records from one DNS server. The UI option to create a new host record is disabled.
artifact: "New Host (A or AAAA)..." is greyed out on DNS server DC2
Zone type on DC2 shows the zone is configured as a Secondary zone.
validations: Confirm records can be added on the writable DNS instance.
Confirm changes replicate/transfer to the other server as designed.
Validate resolution for the new record.

triage.q: What should you check FIRST when DNS record creation options are disabled?
options: The zone type (Primary/AD-integrated vs Secondary/read-only)
Forwarders configuration
Reverse lookup zone presence
DHCP scope utilization

diagnosis.q: Why is the record creation option unavailable on this server?
options: The server is hosting a Secondary zone, which is read-only
The DNS cache is full
Clients are using public DNS
The DC is not authorized in Active Directory

fix.q: Which action is the best fix?
options: Add the record on the primary/writable DNS server (or convert to AD-integrated where appropriate)
Delete the DNS zone from all servers and recreate it
Disable recursion on the DNS server
Change DHCP option 003
